quick: 10 mg PO once daily initially; usual 20-40 mg/day (max 80 mg)
Use with caution; generally avoid in newborns/preterm
Reduce starting dose if CrCl <30 (start 5 mg)
summary: Benazepril is an ACE inhibitor used for hypertension, alone or with other agents. It carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity: when pregnancy is detected, discontinue as soon as possible because drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. Key risks are hyperkalemia, renal function decline, cough and angioedema.
indications: Treatment of hypertension in adults and children >=6 years, alone or in combination with other antihypertensives

dosage.d: Initial 10 mg once daily; maintenance 20-40 mg/day in 1-2 doses

dosage.n: Stop diuretic 2-3 days prior if possible to avoid hypotension

dosage.d: Initial 5 mg once daily; titrate to max 40 mg/day
0.2 mg/kg once daily (up to 10 mg); titrate up to 0.6 mg/kg or 40 mg/day
dosage.n: Not for children with GFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2

admin: Take orally once or twice daily, with or without food
If using a diuretic, consider reducing/stopping it before starting to limit first-dose hypotension
Check renal function and potassium within 1-2 weeks of initiation or dose change
An oral suspension may be prepared for patients unable to swallow tablets per label
Discontinue immediately if pregnancy is detected
moa: Benazepril is hydrolyzed to its active metabolite benazeprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme. This reduces conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, lowering vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion, and decreases degradation of bradykinin. The net effect is vasodilation, reduced peripheral resistance and lower blood pressure.

absolute: History of angioedema related to prior ACE inhibitor therapy or hereditary/idiopathic angioedema
Concomitant use of aliskiren in patients with diabetes
Within 36 hours of a neprilysin inhibitor (sacubitril)
relative: Severe aortic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Collagen vascular disease with renal involvement

preg: BOXED WARNING: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue benazepril as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus (oligohydramnios, renal failure, hypotension, skull hypoplasia, fetal/neonatal death).
lact: Minimal amounts are excreted in breast milk in adults. Use with caution; avoid in mothers of newborns and premature infants because of theoretical effects on neonatal renal function and blood pressure.
renal: Reduce the initial dose (start 5 mg) in significant renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min). Monitor potassium and serum creatinine; some patients with renal artery stenosis or volume depletion may develop acute renal failure.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is recommended; the parent drug requires hepatic conversion to benazeprilat, so monitor response in severe hepatic dysfunction.

major: Aliskiren in diabetes - contraindicated (renal impairment, hyperkalemia, hypotension)
Sacubitril/neprilysin inhibitors - angioedema risk; do not co-administer (separate by 36 h)
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes - hyperkalemia
moderate: Other RAAS agents (ARBs) - dual blockade increases hyperkalemia/renal/hypotension risk
NSAIDs - reduced antihypertensive effect and acute renal impairment, especially in elderly/volume-depleted
Diuretics - additive hypotension; mTOR inhibitors - angioedema risk
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; high-potassium salt substitutes can cause hyperkalemia.
interactions.alcohol: Limit; alcohol can increase the blood-pressure-lowering effect.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum potassium, creatinine and BUN; can cause false-positive results in some tests of parathyroid function.

emergency: Anaphylactoid reaction (especially with dialysis membranes or desensitization)

monitoring: Serum potassium at baseline and during therapy (especially with renal impairment, diabetes, K-sparing agents)
Serum creatinine / renal function after initiation and dose changes
Signs of angioedema and, if symptoms warrant, complete blood count
counsel: If you become pregnant or plan to, stop the medicine and contact your provider immediately
Seek emergency care for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or trouble breathing/swallowing
A dry cough is common; report it if bothersome
Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes unless your doctor approves
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; report fainting, especially after the first dose or with dehydration
pk: Antihypertensive effect within 1 hour; peak 2-4 hours
Effective accumulation half-life of benazeprilat approximately 10-11 hours
Blood-pressure effect persists over 24 hours with daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from moisture
pearls: BOXED WARNING: Fetal toxicity - discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected
Prodrug converted to active benazeprilat in the liver
Dry cough is a class effect of ACE inhibitors; switch to an ARB if intolerable
Risk of angioedema is higher in Black patients; treat airway swelling as an emergency
Avoid dual RAAS blockade (with ARB or aliskiren) due to hyperkalemia and renal risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: The most likely manifestation is marked hypotension. Treat with intravenous normal saline to restore blood pressure and supportive care; benazeprilat is poorly removed by hemodialysis. Monitor potassium and renal function.
